title: Honest Hausdorff Inference for Bivariate Causal Benchmark Contours through a Saddle
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4; narrow fixed quadratic saddle benchmark and full-diameter honest radius through block size about 1.7e53; independent validity gate confirms terminal below-floor.
gap_reasons: The delivered theorem matches both minimax criteria at n^(-3/16), but only within a fixed quadratic saddle neighborhood with known uniform design, Gaussian additive errors, and fixed smoothness.

The explicit confidence radius equals the full disk diameter whenever the block size N is at most approximately 1.7×10^53, already from the corner-kernel bias coefficient alone, so the package supplies no useful finite-sample precision for its applied consumer.
The logarithmic comparison establishes improvement over the displayed global-band inversion certificate, not a necessity theorem for every band-based procedure.

The closing 'Honest scope' section incorrectly describes completed proofs and fixed rates as deferred hypotheses; routine editing can resolve that contradiction, but cannot remove the narrow scope or practically vacuous calibration that constrain the projected paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery accepted angle 0 v2, then D0 supplied one derivation and all 13 PR approval items were independently accepted; the maximality audit found the n^-3/16 risk and honest-expected-radius exponent sharp on the unchanged class. D0.5 stopped at incremental below the field floor, chiefly because the class is narrow and the honest radius is full disk diameter through block size about 1.7e53; an independent main validity gate confirmed no bounded same-model repair reaches field. No F-stage or Lean proof was attempted; the residual-scale theorem interface and stale Honest scope prose remain unrepaired in the verbatim artifacts, with the sharper needed scale bound already present in the informal proof.
tldr: A reference-standardized bivariate causal benchmark profile can pass through a saddle, where signed value errors change its local connectivity and ordinary gradient inversion fails. The target is the sharp expected Hausdorff risk and the sharp expected radius of a uniformly 90 percent honest ball on the complete public smooth Gaussian additive class. A localized two-sided comparison, one-sided reference estimation, and feasible residual-scale estimation supply the proposed architecture. The rates and every unavoidable logarithm are outputs of the central question. The applied consumer is a geometric precision benchmark for a published bivariate profile definition, rather than a claim about the assignment law or singularity of the prenatal-alcohol cohort.
gap: Regular contour inference excludes saddle contact, and critical-level volume control does not characterize contour Hausdorff uncertainty. A same-class original-record risk and honest-radius frontier has not been verified in the checked literature.
fill: The sharp-frontier question joins localized geometric propagation, an observable finite-sample certificate, and original Gaussian testing lower bounds, including both signs of the saddle gap and coincidence.
